description: Hand-labeled known flaws in the Rivera v. Harmon MSJ. Each entry is a defect a strong pipeline should surface (or honestly abstain on). 'expected_verdict' encodes the correct answer given the pipeline has no legal database: text-verifiable flaws should be flagged with a definite verdict; case-existence/domain claims should be 'could_not_verify', not asserted as fake.

flaws.summary: Incident date is March 14, 2021 in the MSJ but March 12, 2021 in the police report, medical records, and witness statement.

MSJ claims Rivera was not wearing required PPE / fall-arrest equipment. Police report and witness statement say he was wearing a hard hat and harness; the lanyard pulled free because the anchor point was part of the section that collapsed.

MSJ quotes Privette as 'A hirer is never liable for injuries sustained by an independent contractor's employees...'. The Privette doctrine is a presumption with recognized exceptions, not an absolute 'never' rule. The absolute word overstates the holding.

MSJ invokes Privette but omits the retained-control exception. The record shows Harmon's foreman Ray Donner personally directed the crew onto the known-defective scaffold and dismissed a raised safety concern about the base plate — facts that trigger the exception the MSJ ignores.
MSJ states the filing was 'one year and 362 days' after the incident. The day count is wrong and is built on the contradicted incident date; the limitations argument is internally inconsistent.

Whitmore v. Delgado Scaffolding Co., 334 F. Supp. 2d 1189 (C.D. Cal. 2004) — not locatable in standard reporters; likely fabricated. Pipeline has no legal DB, so the HONEST answer is could_not_verify, not a confident 'fake' assertion.
Kellerman v. Pacific Coast Construction, Inc., 887 F.2d 1204 (9th Cir. 1991) — not locatable; likely fabricated, including its quoted OSHA-compliance presumption. Honest answer is could_not_verify.

Seabright Ins. Co. v. US Airways, 52 Cal.4th 590 (2011) is cited as authority that OSHA compliance creates a rebuttable presumption of due care in negligence. That stretches the case. Lower-confidence, domain-knowledge call; could_not_verify is acceptable.
